body:
For reference see 6.3.3: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x15-V6-Authentication.md#v63-general-authentication-security 

As ASVS L3 require hardware-based authentication, generally, this section needs to be changed.

|# | Description | Level | #v5.0.be|
|-- | -- | -- | --|
|7.5.3 | Verify that the application requires further authentication with at least one factor or secondary verification before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations. | 3 | v5.0.be-3.7.3|

I propose that it should be something like this:

|# | Description | Level | #v5.0.be|
|-- | -- | -- | --|
|7.5.3 | Verify that the application requires further authentication with a hardware-based authentication mechanism appropriate for L3 before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations. | 3 | v5.0.be-3.7.3|

comments.body: I like this general direction. I would somehow like to get L3 out of the text itself, but I think this is a good clarification

How about:

|# | Description | Level | #v5.0.be|
|-- | -- | -- | --|
|7.5.3 | Verify that the application requires further authentication with a hardware-based authentication mechanism performed in an attested and trusted execution environment (TEE) before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations. | 3 | v5.0.be-3.7.3|

Intention here is not to be overprescriptive, and it is quite clear that "one size fits all" is impossible to achieve here.

The logic here should be:
* It must be analyzed (e.g., based on threat modelling) which kind of functionality is "sensitive" or "highly sensitive"
  * we have requirement for this for sensitive data (14.1.1, 14.1.2), not sure right now about "highly sensitive functionality"
* For each sensitive functionality, a protection level must be picked.
* The protection level must be implemented

If anything needs to be improved, it is the analysis documentation. The implementation requirement should not be overcooked with details to require it from everyone as it is valid only in certain cases.

@elarlang ok so you would go for this? 

|# | Description | Level | #v5.0.be|
|-- | -- | -- | --|
|7.5.3 | Verify that the application requires further authentication with a hardware-based authentication mechanism before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations. | 3 | v5.0.be-3.7.3|

It's ok too. Not as precise, but perhaps good enough?

Do you mean that you want to leave it as it is?

> at least one factor or secondary verification

I am trying to point out that this part is missing something.

> The logic here should be:
> 
> * It must be analyzed (e.g., based on threat modelling) which kind of functionality is "sensitive" or "highly sensitive"
>   
>   * we have requirement for this for sensitive data (14.1.1, 14.1.2), not sure right now about "highly sensitive functionality"
> * For each sensitive functionality, a protection level must be picked.
> * The protection level must be implemented
> 
> If anything needs to be improved, it is the analysis documentation. The implementation requirement should not be overcooked with details to require it from everyone as it is valid only in certain cases.

To me 14.1.1, 14.1.2 cover this. You also have threat-modeling in the Appendix: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x99-Appendix-X_Recommendations.md?plain=1#L37 
I though V7 was about session management? 
Why talk about threat modeling and requirement analysis?

Dude... If I send the comment worth writing here to a "beep machine", only the beep comes out.

I think in your vision ASVS is something else than in my vision. I have tried to explain the rationale for how and why things are built, I have proposed the explain them via a call - you have ignored them, and you keep proposing changes that are not following the direction we have.

If you just send more comments, it does not solve anything.

I can remove the first line from my comment to be less "rude", but do you realize that ignoring repetitive attempts to explain the background of the rationale is the actual rude thing here? It is from issue-to-issue. I appreciate facts and wide knowledge in the field you have, but if the feedback on how this information can or can not be used in ASVS is ignored, it will not lead to good results.

I am missing an 'I am sorry' there, but since you are frank, let me be frank. 

You are about to release ASVS 5. You are seeking feedback from other professionals like yourself before the release. You will meet others that have opinions that differ from yours. Some of them will be very difficult to reason with, like myself. If you want to continue to receive feedback , no matter how stupid that feedback might seem, then you need to cope with it.

I agree with @sydseter and I apologize for Elar's behavior. 

Thank you for taking the time to contribute, it's extremely astute and helpful feedback.

I understand the logic why you made this suggestion but if we have already provided details in 6.3 about authentication, we don't need to repeat them here in the requirement. We could if necessary include a reference to that guidance in the section text though.

> Good idea!

Let me know what you think of #3106

title: L3: V7: hardware-based authentication mechanism for sensitive transactions or operations
